content.body: That way, I can hopefully get alerted to checker breakage before any spec editors do — or at least at around the same time any editors might start running into it — and start right away on fixing the checker before more editors are affected.
Context is that yesterday, both the WebExtensions and WebDriver spec builds broke because the Bikeshed output had some CSS stuff that I hadn’t yet taught to the checker.
…And I only found out about it because of getting Cc‘ed on issues from those spec repos.

As a community member who contributes to web standards because of the community feeling: it makes me sad to see human interaction fade away with more and more of my PRs to web standards reviewed only by AI. It removes the human aspect of the "web community" for me and makes it less enjoyable to contribute and more of a chore. I don't get paid to do this, so my own motivation keeps me going. AI reviews don't help with that.

No need to start a whole debate about this. Only wanted to share my current feeling and needed to write it in a place where I know humans read the actual stuff. Thanks for reading humans, would love to continue reading your not-so-perfect sentences. Please continue your day as you were planning to.
